evidence_scope: 25 original frames each; derived 148px previews approximate renderer translation and two halo passes, Pillow bicubic differs from Compose Medium filtering; static custom app palette, not dynamic system colors. Anchor sums vectorized float32 approximate Kotlin sequential float accumulation.

reviewers.evidence_scope: 15 supplied botanical bloom animations; all 375 source frames viewed in original 5x5 sheets, then all 375 in each of the light and dark 148px corrected contact sheets.
shared_findings: Fix hard asset defects first: Magnolia has duplicated subjects and broken bands; Fuchsia and Iris have background-colored holes through intended petal surfaces. No timing or glow treatment can repair those surfaces.

Every progress frame should change a readable growing structure: seed crack, attached stem, leaf unfurling, bud swelling, petal separation, or final center reveal. Fine repainting of a static bud contributes little at the actual viewing size.
The first-row-to-second-row boundary often resets growth; F5→6 should be checked as carefully as the final opening. Snowdrop even loses an apparent early bud there.

Plant identity must persist: keep each leaf junction, branch, bud and flower attached to the same location. Chocolate Cosmos and Snowdrop currently move or replace already open flowers, and Queen of the Night introduces unexplained late buds.

Use a stable seed/base shape and authored anchor. Runtime bottom-band correction can reduce translation, but cannot fix seed resizing, branch replacement or silhouette changes; its measured anchor range is not a pure motion metric.

Reserve safe margins after runtime correction and halo. Source clipping is visible on Jade Vine; approximate corrected previews also cut top details in several otherwise intact sheets. This requires actual Compose verification before declaring a fix.
Do not reserve all meaningful flower opening for F21–25. Passionflower, Bee Orchid and Iris spend too many frames in a near-held bud, then rush the most rewarding anatomy.
At 148px, value structure beats intricate texture: fewer separated Jade Vine claws, somewhat larger Myosotis faces, and brighter broad Chocolate Cosmos petal planes would communicate more clearly.
Perceptually redundant means near-held/repainted, not literally identical pixels. The parent evidence check reports no exact adjacent RGBA duplicate frames.
Final-frame impact should come from a complete, readable blossom and deliberate settling, not an abrupt whole-object zoom or surprise new branches. Preserve the calm character of the brewing flow.

reviewers.evidence_scope: All 15 original 1280x1280 sheets and all 30 corresponding 148px light/dark labeled contact sheets were inspected visually, covering all 375 source frames. Frame references are 1-based, 5x5 row-major. Contact sheets approximate the current anchor translation and silhouette halos using Pillow bicubic; actual device pixels depend on density and the app uses a different sampling filter. Live Compose playback was not observed. No literal adjacent duplicate claims: near-holds refer to perceptual redundancy. Priorities concern progression, not wholesale replacement of final artwork.
shared_findings: Every original sheet was visually inspected; no claims are based only on asset names or generation prompts.

The strongest improvement is temporal continuity: keep the same bean, stem, branches, petals, and fruit nodes across frames. Runtime translation can correct position but cannot repair anatomy replacements or growth reversal.

Several flower and magical sheets reach a convincing finish around F15-20 and spend the final frames on contour/texture redraws. Reallocate those frames to visible development, then use a small final settle.
Fruit sheets have richer narrative milestones but frequently introduce mature fruit at new positions. Earlier buds must establish the later harvest layout.
F5→6 and F20→21 deserve explicit checks because several row boundaries visibly reset growth or ripeness. Not every sheet has a row-boundary fault.
Preserve strong final artwork. Rebuild means restructuring the progression around it, not necessarily regenerating the entire visual style.
A useful frame changes one readable structural feature while preserving everything already grown; tiny sparks, texture variation, and petal repainting are weak substitutes at small display sizes.

Both light and dark 148px contact sheets were reviewed for every assigned id. Pale flowers remain readable through their outlines; luminous thin steam/loops lose more weight in light theme. These are approximate composites, not live Compose screenshots.

Possible faint source-cell residue was visually observed near jasmine F12-14, latte F19-20, and coffee_plant F7. Confirm with source alpha/component inspection before treating these as proven cleanup defects.

reviewers.evidence_scope: Read-only visual review of all 14 original 1280x1280 sheets, every row-major F1-F25 cell, and all 28 derived 148px light/dark composites using approximate current per-frame anchor translation and two halo passes. No live Compose playback, device-density, timing, or reduced-motion proof.

shared_findings.finding: Repeated middle poses make the animation feel stalled, then rushed.
shared_findings.evidence: Across most assigned sheets, roughly F11-20 retain a closed bud or sphere with texture/scale changes; F21-23 then carry most opening. Dahlia opens slightly earlier at F19-20 and bat flower at F17-20.
shared_findings.recommendation: Replace near-held middle poses with identifiable seam release, petal unfolding and center reveal. A frame should advance silhouette, anatomy or a prepared light/reveal event, not just redraw texture.

shared_findings.finding: Theme-dependent holes are source-art problems, not simply low contrast.
shared_findings.evidence: King protea, foxglove, cherry blossom, water lily, stained-glass iris, aurora anemone and constellation have areas that look like highlights on light but become background on dark. Morning glory additionally has large missing horizontal bands.
shared_findings.recommendation: Inspect recoverable pre-matting images and alpha masks before regenerating art. Keep petal surfaces intact and validate on both actual theme backgrounds; do not compensate by making halos stronger.

shared_findings.evidence: Foxglove F21 lower bell is absent F22; water lily center visible F23 hidden F24 returns F25; iris front lower petal disappears/relocates F24; moonphase and constellation partly close F24; pincushion raises then removes a central cone F24-25.
shared_findings.recommendation: Track the same petal/bell/center structures across frames, with monotonic opening until a small deliberate settling motion. Finish on an earned stable shape.

shared_findings.finding: Exact valid PNG geometry is insufficient for a usable animation.
shared_findings.evidence: Morning glory shows more than one plant in several actual cells, horizontal cutouts and detached fragments despite being a nominal five-by-five image.
shared_findings.recommendation: Review all 25 independently cropped cells as well as the sheet; enforce one continuous plant, no neighboring-frame remnants and consistent registration.

shared_findings.finding: Strong concepts survive at the intended small size.
shared_findings.evidence: Dahlia's coral layers, pincushion's orange arcs, Himalayan lantern's shell reveal, crema's curls and moonphase's ivory sphere/flower are clear on both 148px composites.
shared_findings.recommendation: Preserve these palettes and silhouettes. Spend effort on meaningful growth and anatomical continuity rather than adding particles, extra decoration, controls or more intricate texture.

shared_findings.finding: The current halo makes subtle outline artifacts visible, but it cannot hide major content problems.
shared_findings.evidence: Approximate composites show gray or pale rims around some plants; dark bat flower detail still recedes and missing petal regions still change the flower between themes.
shared_findings.recommendation: Repair assets first, then judge the halo at actual density and in the full UI. Keep contrast correction restrained and only as strong as needed for shape readability.

review.strength: The ivory flower against the glossy coffee bean is immediately readable; the broad five-petal finish is a strong, restrained reward.
issues: F1-4 mostly changes the bean seam brightness; the silhouette offers little progress before F5.
F10-16 grows the bud clearly, but F17-19 spends three frames on nearly the same cupped shape.
F23→24 replaces the cupped flower with a front-facing five-petal layout in one step; the large lower petals arrive abruptly. F24-25 then adds very little.
review.recommendation: Keep the final flower and bean. Redistribute two near-hold frames into intermediate outward/downward petal rotations before F24; track the same five petals from closed bud to finish. Make seam separation, rather than brightness alone, carry the early progress.
review.confidence: High for sheet anatomy and frame progression; playback pacing unobserved.
review.small_size_assessment: Clear in both themes at 148px. Light-theme outlines preserve the ivory petals; the final five-petal silhouette reads more strongly than the earlier cup. The F23→24 change remains conspicuous at this scale.

review.strength: The luminous loops and surrounding stars create a recognizable magical identity with excellent large-shape contrast on dark backgrounds.
issues: F4→5 jumps rapidly from an opening bean to a nearly full-height plume.
F5-9 largely redraws the plume; stars appear at F8 and disappear at F9 rather than establishing a growing constellation.
F15-18 already has the three-loop flower and four surrounding stars. F19-25 mostly removes the remaining top wisp and shuffles small details; completion has little new payoff.
Thin loop interiors and tiny sparks compete with the central motif rather than contributing equally useful progress.
review.recommendation: Rebuild the progression around a persistent three-loop constellation while retaining the final palette and bean. Let a short plume trace the left, right, then top loop over distinct intervals; reveal stars only as their matching loop completes. Save closure of the top loop and one coherent final light expansion for F23-25.
review.confidence: High for progression redundancy and discontinuous stars; light/dark contact sheets reviewed, playback unobserved.
review.small_size_assessment: Excellent dark-theme readability. In light theme the loops/stars become fine outlined shapes and lose luminous impact, though still identifiable. A slightly stronger warm-gold edge on the major loops would help more than extra sparks.

review.strength: The cream rosetta has an elegant, clean silhouette and a strong coffee-specific association; it needs very little extra decoration.
issues: F5-9 repeats a tall steam shape without a clear transition toward the rosetta.
F10 has a broad cream surface and tall plume, then F11 collapses to a short sideways curl: a clear visual regression at the row boundary.
F13-15 adds most of the rosetta lobes quickly. F16-25 is essentially the finished leaf, with tip and contour repainting instead of meaningful growth.
review.recommendation: Rebuild the middle and late progression using one continuous rosetta stem. Eliminate the F10→11 reset, add alternating cream lobes one pair at a time, and reserve the top lobe and final broadening for the last quarter. Preserve the restrained final artwork.
review.confidence: High; major silhouette regression and prolonged finish are directly visible.
review.small_size_assessment: The rosetta remains readable in both themes, with stronger impact on dark. F16-25 feels particularly static at 148px. F19-20 also shows faint horizontal stray marks above the main art in the supplied composites; verify and clear source-cell residue.

review.strength: The four broad glossy leaves read clearly, and the bean-to-sprout story is direct without requiring flower details.
issues: F6→7 makes a large stem-height step while F7-9 changes little except tiny leaves.
F11→12 shrinks the established leaf pair; F13 enlarges it again, producing a growth reversal.
F15-18 shows a small paired shoot at the top, but F19 replaces it with a flat, cut-looking stem tip.
F19-24 offers almost the same two-tier plant, and F25 simply enlarges leaves. The final tip remains visually unfinished.
review.recommendation: Repair the leaf-size reversal and carry the top shoot continuously into a small third leaf pair. Keep the two mature tiers stable while the new pair separates during F20-24; finish with a naturally tapered growing tip instead of a flat stump.
review.confidence: High; explicit anatomy reversals visible.
review.small_size_assessment: Leaf tiers read well in both themes. The F11→12 shrink and lost top leaves at F19 are obvious at 148px. A faint isolated horizontal mark is visible above F7; verify/clear source-cell residue.

review.strength: The combination of yellow flowers, green fruit, and bright red tomatoes gives excellent narrative variety and a visually generous final reward.
issues: F1→2 abruptly rotates the bean from diagonal to upright; this reads as an object replacement without an intermediate turn.
F5→6 loses the developing branched tip and returns to a simpler single sprout.
F12→13 adds several substantial branches/leaves at once; F15→16 changes branch geometry while introducing the first flower and fruit.
F20→21 turns the upper ripe red tomato back into green and rearranges the lower clusters.
F24-25 has a compelling full harvest, but late fruits appear in new positions instead of consistently growing from established flowers.
review.recommendation: Lock the bean orientation and main branch skeleton. Keep every fruit attached to the same node through green enlargement and red ripening; repair the F20→21 reverse-ripening first. Stage the two major lower clusters over the final six frames rather than adding a new harvest arrangement at the end.
review.confidence: High for visible fruit continuity and row-boundary regressions.
proposed_milestones: F17 flowers and tiny green fruit
review.small_size_assessment: The final red fruit is clear in both themes. Mid-sequence green fruit competes with tiny leaves, so fewer stable clusters with clean gaps would communicate progress better than added fine detail.

review.strength: The four large red berries and surviving white flower form one of the clearest final compositions; the triangular berry shape remains distinctive.
issues: F1→2 changes bean orientation abruptly. F5→6 shortens the sprout after the first leaf pair has appeared.
F11→12 adds a large flower and substantial lower foliage in one step; the flower also moves toward the center in F13.
F15→16 removes/rearranges several flowers while introducing sizeable green berries, obscuring flower-to-fruit continuity.
F21→22 introduces a new lower-right green berry without an earlier visible flower at that node; the final four-fruit layout is only established late.
review.recommendation: Keep the strong final layout but establish its four fruit nodes before flowering. Show each white flower closing into a small green berry at the same location, then enlarge and redden the berries on a staggered schedule. Repair the early sprout reset and stabilize the bean.
review.confidence: High for growth and node continuity; final berry shape confirmed readable in both 148px theme composites.
review.small_size_assessment: One of the strongest final silhouettes at 148px: four red berries remain separately recognizable in both themes. Seed detail remains a texture rather than a required cue; preserve the large berry shapes and spacing.

review.strength: The red compound berries contrast strongly with the leaves; the fruiting cane gives a richer endpoint than a simple single flower.
issues: F1→2 changes bean orientation abruptly; the soil ring and bean texture continue to shift later.
F7→8 adds a large amount of foliage in one step; F10→11 introduces a prominent white flower while reshaping the canopy.
F12-17 already has the right fruiting branch but spends several frames moving small green berries around instead of clearly enlarging fixed berries.
F19→20 suddenly adds multiple large red berries, including a left berry. F23→24 substantially rearranges the fruit clusters, and F25 adds more fruit again.
review.recommendation: Retain the recognizable raspberry texture but lock one cane and two fruiting branches. Establish all final berry nodes as buds by mid-sequence, grow them in place, and reserve ripening for the last third. Rework F19-25 as one coherent staggered harvest instead of several alternate final compositions.
review.confidence: High for changing cluster layout; botanical realism is not being asserted.
review.small_size_assessment: Red berries and their compound texture remain recognizable in both themes, but tiny green berries/branchlets merge with leaves. Stable cluster locations and clear berry-to-leaf gaps matter more than fine thorns or vein detail.

review.strength: The bell-shaped flowers and powdery blue fruit give this animation a distinctive identity; the simple oval leaves avoid some of the visual clutter of other fruit plants.
issues: F1→2 changes bean orientation and F5→6 shortens the seedling.
F10→11 adds several developed flowers abruptly; later flowers move between branches instead of consistently becoming fruit.
F18→19 turns several right berries blue in one step; F20→21 suddenly introduces a larger multi-berry arrangement and fruit on the left.
F22-25 mostly repaints/repositions already mature berries, with little remaining growth and some changing overlap.
review.recommendation: Preserve the airy leaves and bell flowers. Establish the final two berry clusters earlier, transition each flower through a small green sphere, and stagger the blue color change. Spend F22-25 on the last berries reaching size/color while already ripe berries remain fixed.
review.confidence: High for observed cluster and ripening changes; both 148px theme composites reviewed.
review.small_size_assessment: Blue fruit remains distinct from green leaves in both themes; the pale bell flowers read especially well on dark. Final overlapping berries are understandable as a cluster, but successive redraws produce little useful change at 148px.

review.strength: The green-to-red-to-purple ripening story is strong, and the pale blossom provides a helpful contrasting focal point above the dark fruit.
issues: F1→2 rotates the bean; F5→6 offers little additional silhouette development.
F10→11 swaps a leafy tip for an open flower without a clear bud-opening bridge.
F17→18 jumps from green to substantially larger red berries; F19 adds a large left fruit that was not established as a visible earlier bud.
F20→21 makes nearly the whole crop dark at once and relocates the upper cluster. F21-25 mainly shifts the finished berries and foliage.
F21-25 dark fruit is visually quieter than the red stage. It remains recognizable in the 148px dark composite, but stronger fruit-to-leaf gaps would preserve the final harvest emphasis.
review.recommendation: Track four persistent fruit nodes from bud to green, red, and purple. Use the final five frames to ripen those nodes sequentially, preserve berry positions, and give the dark berries a slightly broader cool highlight and clear negative space from the bean/leaves.
review.confidence: High for sequence continuity; dark fruit remains identifiable in supplied 148px dark-theme approximation.
review.small_size_assessment: The dark fruit is still recognizable with the existing highlights/halo in the dark composite, but visually quieter than the red ripening stage. Keep clear gaps around fruit and broad highlights; do not brighten the whole asset or add more detail.

review.strength: The warm steam/flame and opened bean are bold and readable, with a compact symmetric silhouette suited to a small brewing display.
issues: F4→5 suddenly establishes a tall plume; F5-7 then changes mainly its contour.
F10→11 reduces the size/height of the steam and side curls at the row boundary.
F13-15 reaches the complete three-pronged steam motif. F16-25 largely repaints that same state and tiny sparks.
The final shape is visually close to coffee_starlit, reducing the distinction between the two choices; its finish has little new event.
review.recommendation: Rebuild the timing around a continuous brewing plume while preserving the bean and colors. Let the side curls form gradually and rise/relax into a single coherent steam crown only near completion. Avoid star-like additions here so starlit owns the constellation finish; reserve the final frames for a readable final expansion and settle.
review.confidence: High for long visual plateau and F10→11 shrink; relative theme identity is aesthetic judgment.
review.small_size_assessment: Main curls remain readable, especially on dark. Light theme reduces them to pale thin contours, weakening visual impact; strengthen selected warm-gold boundaries rather than expanding the halo or adding sparks.

review.strength: The saturated red, layered bloom is immediately recognizable and creates a strong focal point without relying on particles.
issues: F2-4 uses a bright red/orange seam flare that disappears when the sprout arrives at F5, adding an isolated effect rather than continuous growth.
F10→11 is nearly a hold, then F11→12 enlarges the red bud substantially in one step.
F17→18 changes a narrow upright bud into a broad, more front-facing rose abruptly.
F20-25 is already fully open and mostly redraws the petal spiral, with little distinguishable progress.
review.recommendation: Keep the final rose. Redistribute late near-holds into intermediate opening poses between F12-20, tracking the same outer petal edges as they roll outward. Save the last outer-petal layer and gentle final widening for F23-25, and soften the isolated early flare.
review.confidence: High for silhouette transitions and late redundancy.
review.small_size_assessment: Strong in both themes at 148px. Red and the broad whorled silhouette carry the identity; late internal petal redraws add little at this size. No extra particles or ornament are needed.

review.strength: The broad layered ivory flower gives a calm, luminous finish, and the low bloom positioned near the bean feels balanced.
issues: F9→10 changes a small green bud into a substantially larger white bud in one step.
F10-13 repeats a similar closed bud with only minor contour changes.
F15-18 spends four frames in a similar cup shape; F19→20 then adds a visibly new lower petal tier abruptly.
F21-25 has nearly the same fully opened silhouette, with petal rearrangement rather than a distinct final opening.
review.recommendation: Preserve the layered finish but distinguish the tiers from the bud stage onward. Open the outer tier first, then the inner tier, with a persistent petal count/layout. Use the spare closed-bud and final-hold frames to bridge F19→20 and reveal the center only near completion.
review.confidence: High for tier appearance and redundant ranges.
review.small_size_assessment: The broad layered silhouette is clear in both themes. Light theme relies on gold outlines for inner-tier separation; preserve those boundaries. Most F21-25 differences become negligible at this scale.

review.strength: One of the clearest sequences in this set: a round bud opens into a dark disk with bright yellow rays, and the radial silhouette stays recognizable at a glance.
issues: F10→11 and F16→17 contribute little visible progress relative to adjacent steps.
F12→13 exposes much of the disk at once; a partial sepal-opening bridge would help.
F20-25 is effectively the mature flower, with slight petal redraws/scale changes rather than a purposeful final phase.
The bean seam flare F2-4 is more visually active than some later growth steps.
review.recommendation: Polish the existing sequence rather than redesign it. Move one near-hold into the first disk reveal, keep the disk/petal arrangement fixed, and distribute the final ray-petal extension across F20-24 before a stable F25. Reduce incidental texture changes.
review.confidence: High for relative clarity and redundant late frames; playback smoothness unobserved.
review.small_size_assessment: Best immediate small-size recognition in this group: dark disk, yellow rays, and green leaves are distinct in both themes. Final-frame redraws are barely meaningful, so continuity and timing are the priority.

review.strength: The mature white orchid is elegant and distinctive, with a broad silhouette and colored lip that provide a clear visual reward.
issues: F10-16 reads as a generic upright cup-shaped flower rather than an emerging orchid; most identity arrives very late.
F18→19 replaces the cup center with a detailed orchid lip and changes the side petals/front-facing geometry in one jump.
F19-25 is largely the completed orchid, with scale and small lip/petal redraws consuming the final quarter.
The subtle pale petal veins and small colored center will contribute less than the broad silhouette at app size.
review.recommendation: Keep the mature orchid but rebuild F12-21 around its actual final petal arrangement: two broad side petals gradually separate and the lip unfurls downward from a persistent center. Spread that reveal over several frames and reserve final side-petal expansion for F22-24.
review.confidence: High for visible anatomy discontinuity; not a claim about biological timing.
review.small_size_assessment: The final broad side petals identify the flower in both themes; the small colored lip remains visible but subtle. F18→19 is still a conspicuous design change at 148px. Preserve broad petal separation rather than increasing vein detail.

review.strength: The final five-petal white star is simple, bright, and readable; the restrained palette works well with the coffee bean.
issues: F12-14 has thin stray horizontal colored pixels visible above the bud in the original sheet; inspect and clear the affected cell margins.
F12-18 closely resembles the coffee_flower cup sequence, delaying jasmine's own narrow/star-shaped identity.
F19-22 moves through a bent, roughly four-lobed layout; F23 introduces a five-petal layout and F25 rearranges it again. The flower reads as changing designs rather than the same petals unfolding.
F20→21 mainly holds the earlier asymmetric form, leaving too few frames to resolve the final star continuously.
review.recommendation: Clean the stray pixels and establish five persistent narrow petals in the closed bud. Unfold those same petals outward in a stable order from F15 onward, keeping the flower center and leaf positions fixed. Preserve the final star but bridge its lower petals over several frames.
review.confidence: High for visible late petal-layout changes; stray pixels observed in original rendering and should be confirmed by alpha inspection.
review.small_size_assessment: The final star is readable in both themes, but the preceding four-lobed/asymmetric forms make late progression feel like a changing flower design. F12-14 faint horizontal residue is also visible in the contact sheets.

review.strength: The arched pink heart raceme and white hanging tips are distinctive; F12–20 visibly develop the flower rather than just increasing scale.
issues: F1→2 rotates a flat bean into an upright split seed without an intermediate; F5→6 removes the paired seed leaves and shortens the plant.
F10→11 substantially enlarges and repositions the lower foliage; F11→12 replaces the right leafy branch with a flowering raceme instead of retaining a clear branch-to-bud transition.
F15→16 shifts the plant left and changes the bean size; F18→19 introduces an already flowering left raceme. These read as composition changes rather than continuous growth.

F21–25 are nearly the same finished arrangement with small repaint/pose differences, while the hanging hearts crowd the horizontal bounds. Extra flower count is less valuable than readable heart silhouettes at 148px.
review.recommendation: Keep the final heart design; rebuild only the structural transitions using fixed bean and branch landmarks. Carry seed leaves through F5–7, establish the left raceme as tiny buds before F18, and use the last five frames for sequential heart swelling and white-tip emergence on existing stalks.
review.confidence: High for static anatomy, continuity and perceptual holds across all 25 frames; medium for runtime clipping/feel because theme composites approximate Compose and actual playback was not observed.
proposed_milestones: F1–5 crack and rooted paired leaves
F6–10 continuous arch and permanent foliage
F11–15 visible buds on both racemes
F16–20 hearts inflate and tips release
F21–25 finish distal hearts without adding or moving branches
review.small_size_theme_review: At 148px the pink hearts remain readable in both themes, but the final cluster becomes crowded and the approximate corrected preview cuts the highest foliage at F21–25. Preserve gaps between hearts and leave post-correction top margin.

evidence.frames_visually_reviewed: F1–25 row-major; all four row boundaries compared

review.strength: The final white petals, purple radial corona and raised green center form an excellent distinctive payoff; the curled tendrils provide a recognizable vine accent.
issues: F1–3 mostly alter the seed crack; F5→6 reduces the visible sprout, losing early progress.
F10→11 jumps to a taller plant with a definite terminal bud; F12–18 repeatedly repaint an almost unchanged closed bud. F15→16 adds little visible progress.
F20→21 begins the actual opening very late. F23→24 suddenly reveals a fully formed raised center while the bean visibly shrinks and the composition changes.
F24→25 is predominantly enlargement; the most interesting corona separation is compressed into F21–24.
review.recommendation: Preserve the final flower and allocate more frames to its opening: begin sepal separation around F14, reveal the corona progressively around F17–21, and grow the center through F22–25. Hold the bean, leaf junctions and flower attachment fixed while opening.
review.confidence: High for static anatomy, continuity and perceptual holds across all 25 frames; medium for runtime clipping/feel because theme composites approximate Compose and actual playback was not observed.
proposed_milestones: F6–10 leaves, tendrils and bud stalk
F11–15 bud swelling and first sepal separation
F16–20 petal fan and corona expansion
F21–25 center rises and flower settles
review.small_size_theme_review: At 148px the final corona/center is still readable on both themes. The near-held F12–18 buds are especially apparent, and the approximate corrected preview clips the top of the F12–15 buds.

evidence.frames_visually_reviewed: F1–25 row-major; all four row boundaries compared

review.strength: The pink three-part silhouette and dark patterned lip give a clear, charming identity once open.
issues: F1→2 changes the seed orientation; F5→6 lowers the sprout/base composition.
F8→9 introduces both large leaves in one step; F12→13 jumps from a small green tip to a large pink bud.
F13–18 hold nearly the same closed bud, including the F15→16 row transition; most differences are contour and paint changes.

F20→21 exposes most of the dark lip in one step; F21→22 suddenly spreads both lateral petals. F23–25 increasingly enlarge the flower while shrinking the bean, creating a zoom-like finish instead of further opening.
review.recommendation: Retain the finished orchid; replace redundant bud frames with leaf unfurling and staged lateral-petal/lip release. Fix bean scale and flower center, then finish by rounding the patterned lip and settling the three petals.
review.confidence: High for static anatomy, continuity and perceptual holds across all 25 frames; medium for runtime clipping/feel because theme composites approximate Compose and actual playback was not observed.
proposed_milestones: F11–15 pink bud grows and seams separate
F16–20 lip emerges and side petals lift
F21–25 petals spread and lip rounds at fixed scale
review.small_size_theme_review: At 148px the final lip and pink petals remain clear in both themes. The long bud hold is more obvious than its fine color changes; the approximate corrected preview clips F13–15 bud tips.

evidence.frames_visually_reviewed: F1–25 row-major; all four row boundaries compared

review.strength: Turquoise claw-shaped flowers and a hanging raceme create one of the most unusual and visually rewarding silhouettes in the set.
issues: F5→6 removes the leaves and shortens the vine, an unmistakable reversal.
F9→10 makes a large foliage/stem jump. From about F10 onward the upper stem is visibly cut by the top cell edge, making the plant feel cropped instead of complete.
F10→11 adds a long dangling bud chain; F15→16 jumps from mostly closed narrow buds to many broad hooked flowers at once.

F18–25 add density faster than readable structure. F20→21 shifts/recomposes the bean and raceme, while F23–25 are almost finished-state repetitions with flowers crowded along the right and bottom edges.
review.recommendation: Rebuild the composition with a complete curved vine inside a consistent safe margin. Preserve the claw design and turquoise color, reduce competing tendril detail, and open a fixed set of raceme buds in a clear top-to-bottom wave.
review.confidence: High for static anatomy, continuity and perceptual holds across all 25 frames; medium for runtime clipping/feel because theme composites approximate Compose and actual playback was not observed.
proposed_milestones: F1–5 stable seed and leafy vine tip
F11–15 fixed hanging bud chain develops
F21–25 lower claws finish with clear gaps
review.small_size_theme_review: At 148px the turquoise color reads well, but the tendrils, leaves and many claws compete for attention. Top clipping persists in both themes; fewer, more separated claws would be clearer.

evidence.frames_visually_reviewed: F1–25 row-major; all four row boundaries compared

review.strength: The final orange fan against a blue spear has strong color contrast and an immediately readable directional silhouette.
issues: F1→2 flips the seed orientation; F5→6 lowers the sprout. F8→9 produces the paired leaves abruptly.
F11→13 transforms the upright tip into the large horizontal sheath over very few frames.
F13–18 largely hold the horizontal green sheath, with only tiny tip-color changes; F15→16 actually appears to reduce the orange opening.
F20→21 adds much of the orange crest; F21→22 changes the supporting leaves and stem bend. F23–25 mostly enlarge/spread the completed flower as the bean shrinks.
review.recommendation: Keep the final orange/blue silhouette; spend F13–20 opening the sheath and lifting individual orange segments with the blue spear emerging between them. Lock the stem bend, leaves and seed scale through the finish.
review.confidence: High for static anatomy, continuity and perceptual holds across all 25 frames; medium for runtime clipping/feel because theme composites approximate Compose and actual playback was not observed.
proposed_milestones: F6–10 leaf unfolding and stem elongation
F11–15 sheath bends and visibly separates
F16–20 orange segments and blue spear emerge

review.strength: The glass-like color panels and classic upright-and-drooping iris silhouette have strong identity in the final frames.
issues: F8-20 stays a narrow closed lance; color-panel changes substitute for meaningful unfolding across much of the sequence.
F11-25 has numerous jagged background-revealing interruptions through colored petals, so the glass surfaces look broken or missing rather than translucent.
F21-22 leaps from split spear to recognizable iris; F22-23 adds a large frontal drooping petal. That petal disappears or relocates to the side at F24, then returns front-and-center at F25.
Fine multicolored lines become busy texture at 148px, while the overall iris survives. F15-16 has little silhouette change and F20-21 starts the entire reveal late.
review.recommendation: Rebuild affected petal imagery using a stable set of three upright and three descending structures, with intact, clearly bounded glass panels. Open these structures over the middle and late frames while preserving the front fall petal's identity. Simplify internal leading at displayed size.
review.confidence: High: all 25 source frames plus approximate 148px light/dark composites visually inspected. Temporal impression and real Compose rendering remain unverified.
proposed_milestones: F16-20 three fall petals bend downward consistently
F21-25 panels catch light as the stable iris reaches full spread
review.small_size_and_theme: At 148px light exposes pale missing regions among purple panels; dark makes much of the bloom merge into its background. The overall iris is recognizable, but fine leading becomes busy texture and the moving/disappearing front petal is obvious.

review.strength: A simple purple cup becoming a round blue-violet flower with a dark center offers an appealing, readable color contrast.
issues: F6-10 forms a bud well, but F11-21 keeps nearly the same closed oval; F16-20 is especially low-value repainting.
F22 finally exposes the center and F23 abruptly becomes a flat open flower; F23-25 largely repeat this final pose.
F22-25 has conspicuous background-revealing missing bands and patches near petal bases and upper petals; the cyan edges make these look torn rather than luminous.
F5-6 introduces paired leaves and a purple bud at once; F10-11 and F15-16 are minor swelling steps, while F20-21 adds little before the late snap.
review.recommendation: Keep the broad purple petals and dark center. Repair petal surfaces and distribute cup opening across F13-23, preserving petal count and allowing the cyan-to-purple gradient to follow opening surfaces. Finish with a small final spread rather than repeated redraws.
review.confidence: High: all 25 source frames plus approximate 148px light/dark composites visually inspected. Temporal impression and real Compose rendering remain unverified.
proposed_milestones: F16-20 cup widens and center becomes visible
F21-25 petals lower to the open face and settle
review.small_size_and_theme: At 148px light makes the transparent band look like a white petal base; dark makes it a wide missing band around the center. This changes the apparent flower design between themes, beyond a normal contrast variation.

review.strength: Five white petals and sparse gold points give a clean, easily understood flower with a restrained celestial motif.
issues: F9-10 changes a pointed bud into a shorter star-capped shape abruptly; F11-20 then holds a rounded closed bud with minimal new action.
F21 opens two side petals, F22 adds more, and F23 is fully open. F24 raises/recloses front petals before F25 returns to the open five-point silhouette.
F21/F22/F24 show background-revealing holes in white petals, especially the left/top surfaces; cell-boundary specks also appear above the last row.
At 148px the gold nodes remain visible but fine constellation marks are subtle. F15-16 contributes little beyond swelling.
review.recommendation: Keep the five-petal silhouette and restrained gold nodes. Preserve five continuous petal identities, begin separating them earlier, and remove the F24 reclosure. Use a consistent sparse constellation pattern that is uncovered as the petals open, and repair missing white areas.
review.confidence: High: all 25 source frames plus approximate 148px light/dark composites visually inspected. Temporal impression and real Compose rendering remain unverified.
proposed_milestones: F16-20 remaining petals separate and reveal gold nodes
F21-25 all five petals flatten continuously and settle
review.small_size_and_theme: At 148px the five-petal shape and gold nodes read in both themes; connecting marks are subtle. The missing white regions in F21/F22/F24 are much more conspicuous on dark. Preserve a sparse gold motif.
